Zero-based budget   $4,200 fully assigned   Most precise; every dollar has a job   Takes more setup and tracking     Best overall
50/30/20   Needs Wants Savings framework   Simple and fast to maintain   Your fixed costs are too high for a clean 50/30/20 split   Good as a benchmark, not ideal as-is
Cash-envelope style   Cash caps for flexible spending   Strong control for overspending categories   Less useful for fixed bills and digital payments   Good if dining/misc tend to drift
I treated your listed spending as the baseline monthly pattern and assumed the goal is a   practical 3-month plan  , not a debt payoff sprint.
A zero-based budget fits best because:
- Your bills and savings goals are already fairly defined.
- You still have a modest   $325 cushion  , which is worth assigning intentionally.
- It gives the clearest category-by-category plan for the next 3 months.
